module1.title: Password Security & 2FA
module1.description: Why passphrases beat complex short passwords against brute-force attacks, and why 2FA is essential.
module1.takeaway1: Use a 4-5 word passphrase that is easy to visualize but mathematically impossible to guess.
module1.takeaway2: Enable Two-Factor Authentication (2FA/MFA) on your gaming and email accounts as a second defense shield.
module1.takeaway3: Never reuse passwords across different apps; use a secure password manager.
module1.caseStudy: Dimas' gaming account was compromised because he used 'dimas123', the same password from a leaked forum. After enabling 2FA and switching to a passphrase, his account was fully protected.

module2.title: Phishing & Social Engineering
module2.description: Recognizing emotional manipulation tactics that exploit panic, curiosity, or fake prize promises.
module2.takeaway1: If a message promises free prizes but asks for login credentials or fees, it is definitely phishing.
module2.takeaway2: Inspect URLs carefully: scammers use typosquatting domain tricks like 'steancommunity' instead of 'steamcommunity'.
module2.takeaway3: Official services never ask for your password or OTP code over chat or phone.
module2.caseStudy: Sarah received an SMS claiming she won $5,000 and must click a link within 10 minutes. She spotted the suspicious .xyz domain and blocked the sender immediately.

module3.title: Data Privacy & Digital Footprint
module3.description: Protecting personal identity data and understanding that what goes online stays online forever.
module3.takeaway1: Avoid sharing school uniforms with badges, concert tickets with barcodes, or home locations.
module3.takeaway2: Audit phone app permissions: deny location, contacts, or mic access to apps that don't need them.
module3.takeaway3: Your digital footprint is permanent; always think about the future impact before posting.
module3.caseStudy: A photo filter app requested contacts and GPS location. Budi denied the permission since image filters only need photo access.

module4.title: Anti-Cyberbullying & Ethics
module4.description: Cultivating an empathetic digital environment, respecting privacy boundaries, and actionable steps to handle online harassment.
module4.takeaway1: Follow the 4 Defense Steps: Screenshot Evidence -> Don't Retaliate -> Block Bully -> Report to a Trusted Adult.
module4.takeaway2: Don't be a passive bystander; reach out in private to support friends being targeted in group chats.
module4.takeaway3: Creating edited memes of friends without consent violates privacy boundaries and is digital bullying.
module4.caseStudy: When a classmate was mocked in a chat group, Rina didn't join in. She captured screenshot evidence, comforted her friend privately, and reported the incident to the school counselor.

guide.title: Family & Classroom Guide
guide.subtitle: Practical guide for parents and teachers to support children online with safety, empathy, and critical thinking.
guide.parentsTitle: Fostering Open Conversations About Digital Safety at Home
guide.parentsDesc: Rather than confiscating devices and triggering defensive reactions, build shared agreements through supportive and open family dialogues.

parentTips.tip1Desc: If a child accidentally clicks a suspicious link or shares personal details, appreciate their honesty in reporting it instead of reprimanding them.
parentTips.tip2Desc: Designate device-free zones (such as dining tables and bedrooms at bedtime) respected by all household members.
parentTips.tip3Title: Understand Your Child's Gaming & Social Space
parentTips.tip3Desc: Spend 15 minutes playing games together to understand chat features, microtransactions, and in-game friend systems.

parentAgreement.title: Family Digital Safety Charter
parentAgreement.desc: Check off mutual commitments agreed upon with your child. Copy the agreement text to display at home or save in family notes.
parentAgreement.item1: We will never share passwords, OTP codes, or home addresses with anyone on the internet.
parentAgreement.item2: If we see suspicious, weird, or scary messages or links, we will report them immediately to parents without fear of punishment.
parentAgreement.item3: We maintain device-free zones during family meals and 30 minutes before bedtime.
parentAgreement.item4: We will not download new apps or make in-game purchases without discussing them together first.

parentScenarios.title: Critical Digital Incident Response Guide
parentScenarios.desc: Tactical guidance for parents when children face real-world cyber dilemmas or security incidents.
parentScenarios.scenario1Title: Child Clicked a Phishing Link or Entered Account Credentials
parentScenarios.scenario1Do: Validate their courage: 'Thank you for being honest with us.' Immediately change passwords from another device and review recent activity.
parentScenarios.scenario1Dont: Yelling or permanently confiscating the device, which makes children conceal future incidents.
parentScenarios.scenario2Title: Child Witnesses Cyberbullying in a School Group Chat
parentScenarios.scenario2Do: Guide them to take screenshots as evidence, send private words of support to the victim, and inform the school counselor.
parentScenarios.scenario2Dont: Laughing along, forwarding embarrassing photos to others, or escalating retaliation in public chats.
parentScenarios.scenario3Title: Stranger Initiates Friendly Chat & Asks for Private Photos in a Game
parentScenarios.scenario3Do: Reassure the child that they are not to blame. Take control of the device, preserve chat logs, block the user, and report the account.
parentScenarios.scenario3Dont: Blaming the child for playing the game or dismissing stranger contact as harmless chatter.

parentStarters.title: Dinner Table Conversation Starters
parentStarters.desc: Casual prompts to sharpen your child's critical thinking without sounding like an interrogation.
parentStarters.starter1: Why do you think strangers online offer free game currency or prizes to people they don't even know?
parentStarters.starter2: If a friend's social account suddenly started selling cheap phones or asking for urgent money, what do you think happened?
parentStarters.starter3: How much screen break time do you think we need so our eyes and mind stay energized?

eduObjectives.title: Learning Objectives & Digital Literacy Competencies
eduObjectives.desc: Three core competencies students develop through tami's active reasoning methodology.
eduObjectives.obj1Desc: Identify authentic vs deceptive domains, analyze manipulative brand assets, and detect emotional social engineering cues.
eduObjectives.obj2Desc: Calculate passphrase entropy and apply zero-trust evaluation to unsolicited internet links.
eduObjectives.obj3Desc: Understand the permanent nature of digital footprints, protect peer privacy, and assertively stand against cyberbullying.

eduSteps.step1Title: Minutes 00-10: Visual Hook with Threat Detector
eduSteps.step1Desc: Display sample phishing screenshots on the classroom projector. Ask students to spot clues before revealing the answers.
eduSteps.step1Tip: Teacher's Tip: Ask 'What feels off about this screen?' to cultivate sharp, independent observational instincts.
eduSteps.step2Title: Minutes 10-25: Socratic Guided Inquiry with tami
eduSteps.step2Desc: Guide students to consult tami on the chat room to test their reasoning on realistic case scenarios.
eduSteps.step2Tip: Teacher's Tip: Encourage students to ask about real situations they've seen (free diamonds, spam links) to the AI Smart Tutor.
eduSteps.step3Desc: Students test phishing email audits and password entropy calculations in the Practice Lab independently.
eduSteps.step3Tip: Teacher's Tip: Run a mini-competition: 'Who can construct a passphrase with over 80 bits of entropy the fastest?'.
eduSteps.step4Desc: Conclude the session by formulating 3 digital safety rules agreed upon by the entire class.
eduSteps.step4Tip: Teacher's Tip: Encourage students to complete the curriculum quiz to earn their official digital hero certificates.

eduRubric.title: Digital Character & Competency Rubric
eduRubric.desc: Formative assessment rubric for evaluating students' reasoning, ethics, and defensive habits.
eduRubric.row1Developing: Relies solely on logos and visual aesthetics without inspecting the underlying URL domain.
eduRubric.row1Proficient: Automatically verifies domain anatomy, HTTPS certificates, and deceptive TLDs (.xyz, .top).
eduRubric.row2Developing: Uses short passwords with birthdays or easily shares verification codes when pressured.
eduRubric.row2Proficient: Forms high-entropy multi-word passphrases and strictly refuses to share OTP codes with anyone.
eduRubric.row3Developing: Passive or reluctant to report scams and cyberbullying witnessed on social platforms.
eduRubric.row3Proficient: Assertively preserves screenshot evidence, provides moral support to peers, and notifies trusted authorities.
